name: Question 10
problem:
Consider the following statement. 

If $f(x)=2{e}^{4x}+x,$ then $f=O({e}^{4x})$ as $x\to \infty .$

A proof of the statement is given below.

$\text{L1}:\,2{e}^{4x}=O(2{e}^{4x})$  

$\text{L2}:\,{lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{x}{2{e}^{4x}})=0$  

$\text{L3}:\,x=O(2{e}^{4x})$  

$\text{L4}:\,f=O(4{e}^{4x})$  

$\text{L5}:\,f=O({e}^{4x})$  

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.
